arguments.root_cause_explanation: A regional network interruption isolated application capacity from its normal storage path, causing downstream service failures. Metrics (EV003-EV006) showed 100% request error rates for svc-013, svc-016, svc-017, svc-019. Dependencies (EV007, EV010, EV012, EV014) revealed that svc-013 needs svc-007 and svc-012, svc-016 needs svc-015, svc-017 needs svc-011, and svc-019 needs any of svc-008 or svc-017; all those upstream services were unavailable, propagating failure. The initial scan (EV002) identified svc-013, svc-016, svc-017, svc-019 as unavailable. The root cause is therefore the network interruption (H01) that broke storage connectivity and cascaded through dependency chains.
arguments.rationale: The incident began with a regional connectivity event that severed the normal storage path. Evidence from metrics shows all initially failed services had 100% error rates. Dependency inspections traced each failure to upstream services also down, forming a cascade consistent with H01. Repair R04 (cost 8, risk low) fully restored all 16 affected services with zero new outages, matching the requirement for a complete safe repair. Therefore H01 is the correct root cause and R04 the lowest-cost repair achieving full recovery.
